thread:
incident-bot: P1 pager — LyraCorp private VPC: sudden spike in 502s from NLB (us‑east‑1). Alerting on target group unhealthy + DNS timeouts. Paging @network-oncall and @sre-oncall.

jessica (network-oncall): ack — looking. Saw spike starting 04:12 UTC. Do we have healthcheck failures or backend 502 responses?

emily (sre-oncall): both. NLB returning 502s; target group shows healthcheck failures. Also seeing DNS timeouts for lyra.internal.redwood. Could be security group or app-level.

tom (cs-lyra): Lyra says they just rolled a config change touching security groups ~04:10 UTC. They claim rollback completed but traffic still failing.

ryan (infra): Important: is that a customer-managed SG inside their privnet or one we control on the ALB/NLB side? If they changed the app SG we could be seeing blocked healthcheck ports.

jessica: Confirmed customer SG sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h applied at 04:09 UTC. VPC Flow Logs show TCP RST from instance on 8080 when NLB hits healthcheck.

emily: That explains it — NLB healthchecks failing -> targets marked unhealthy -> 502s. Two mitigation options: 1) temporary SG ingress to allow NLB healthcheck IPs/ports; 2) failover customer to dedicated fallback pool (redwood-dedicated-pool-lyra) in another subnet. Which is faster?

tom: Lyra would prefer minimal blast radius — they asked us to open the rule temporarily to restore service while they investigate their deploy.

jessica: I can add precise ingress for NLB healthcheck ports. Need approval from Lyra SRE or CS. Tom, please confirm.

tom: Lyra approves temporary healthcheck exception. Do it.

jessica: Running command now: 
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h --protocol tcp --port 8080 --cidr 10.20.30.0/27 --description "temp allow NLB healthchecks"
```
Applying — will report back in 60s.

incident-bot: jessica updated security group sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h (ingress +tcp 8080 from 10.20.30.0/27). Automated audit note created.

tom: Partial recovery visible — Lyra reports ~70% traffic restored; error rate dropping.

emily: Good. Running target recheck. Some targets still flapping in us-east-1a. Seeing one host not responding to TCP handshake.

lyra-deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T04:08:12Z rolled back at 04:11:03Z; restarted host ip=10.1.5.12 container=api-5f9d.

jessica: One pod on 10.1.5.12 was OOM and stuck -> blocked healthcheck. Lyra restarted that pod per their ops team 04:16 UTC — target moved to healthy.

emily: Marking incident as mitigated at 04:21 UTC but keeping channel open for 30m monitoring. Root cause hypothesis: customer-side SG change blocked NLB healthchecks; secondary factor: single pod OOM prevented full recovery in one AZ.

ryan: Followups: 1) Recommend changing NLB healthcheck to TCP (less app-dependent) or add a lightweight /hc endpoint separate from main app. 2) Consider automated guardrails/alerts when SG changes affect healthchecks. 3) Document dedicated-pool failover steps for Lyra so we can flip if needed.

tom: Lyra requests RCA and a governance plan to avoid accidental SG changes. Also asks for an ops playbook for rapid rollback.

emily: I'll open an incident ticket with timeline and assign to ryan + jessica for remediation tasks. I'll also add CS follow-up with Lyra for RBAC changes on their side.

jessica: I'll tighten the temporary rule after confirming NLB source IP set; then replace broad CIDR with exact NLB IP set in case LB IPs are narrower. Will note change in runbook.

incident-bot: Incident status update: mitigated -> monitoring. Notes: root cause: customer-managed SG change blocked NLB healthchecks causing target group unhealthy -> NLB 502s. Mitigation: temporary SG ingress rule + pod restart. Recommended next steps: dedicated pool fallback playbook, RBAC review, change healthcheck to TCP.

emily (sre-oncall): closing pager handoff to post-incident process. Final check: last 5m error rate back to baseline. We'll keep monitoring and file RCA.

jessica (network-oncall): timeline captured, collecting commands + audit IDs. Will post runbook link in follow-up ticket.

tom (cs-lyra): Customer appreciative of fast response. They want a short summary for their execs. I'll draft and share. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident channel will remain open for 30 minutes for monitoring and then archived. Tagging follow-up ticket: INC-20260317-0421-LYRA
